context: A uni student interviews a retired safety inspector
purpose: Teach: 重量/有害/摂取/歩行/多発/救助/連発/体感

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 長年、現場の安全を見てこられたんですよね。
lines.en: You must have seen a lot of safety work on construction sites over the years.
lines.style: Respectful, genuine curiosity. Lean in slightly. Warm but careful — speaking to someone whose experience matters. Steady eye contact, unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ。重量物の取り扱いで、事故は本当に多発する。
lines.en: Yes. Heavy equipment causes accidents constantly.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, grounded in lived experience. Quiet weight to each word. No dramatics — just stating what decades have taught him. Slight pause after 'Yes' before moving forward.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 有害な粉塵の摂取、現場の課題でしたか。
lines.en: Was dust inhalation a significant problem at your worksites?
lines.style: Thoughtful probe, not interrogation. Lean forward with genuine interest. Voice stays open — asking for him to elaborate, not testing his knowledge. Slight hesitation on 'inhalation,' like searching for the right word.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。歩行スペースを分けることで、ずいぶん減ったよ。
lines.en: Yes. Once we separated the walking paths from the work areas, it dropped considerably.
lines.style: Speaking from memory with quiet satisfaction. Measured pace. A hint of pride in the voice — not boastful, but the understated pleasure of a solution that worked. Trails off slightly, inviting follow-up.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 救助訓練を連発したことも、効果はありましたか。
lines.en: And running rescue drills regularly — that made a difference too?
lines.style: Genuine follow-up, building on what he's said. Leaning in further. Tone is encouraging without being leading — you're asking because you want to understand, not because you're looking for confirmation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 体感で覚えた動きが、実際の場で活きるんだ。
lines.en: When your body learns something through practice, it knows what to do when it actually matters.
lines.style: Gentle wisdom delivered without preaching. Slow, deliberate pace. His voice carries the weight of knowing this is true. No urgency — these are words that have settled in him over time. Soft, grounded finish.
